items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: there was an article that Creed Taylor did on Dad... And Creed was saying that there was a difference between him and Gil Evans.

ctx.x: Wow. I bet the copyists liked your father.

Oh yeah. And he was very neat. It’s interesting, I don’t know if you read, there was an article that Creed Taylor did on Dad and he was talking about Impulse when he first started out. Because “Blues and the Abstract Truth” was one of the original eight albums that they did. Trane had one, J.J. had one, and actually there’s an anniversary set that you can buy with the eight albums on there. And Creed was saying that there was a difference between him and Gil Evans. Dad was very meticulous, very neat and Gil was…
What about song titles? Did he ever have music that he had written, original music, that he had trouble thinking what do I call this?
